draft.title: Incidence and prevalence
card: how much illness there is in a population. Incidence and prevalence are two ways to measure it.
the number of new cases of a condition that start in a set period, such as one year. A person is counted when they first get the condition.
the number of all existing cases, new and old, at one point in time or over a period. A person is counted for as long as they have the condition.
Incidence shows how fast a condition is spreading. Prevalence shows how many people are living with it and how much care they may need.
draft.remember: Incidence is new cases in a period. Prevalence is all cases, new and old.

a.q: A report says 8000 Victorians were newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes last year. Which measure is this?
opts: Incidence, because it counts only new cases in a year
Prevalence, because it counts only new cases in a year
Incidence, because it counts all cases in the population
Prevalence, because it counts all cases in the population
a.why: Only people newly diagnosed in a set period are counted, so this is incidence. Prevalence would also include people diagnosed in earlier years who still have the condition.
a.clue: Are people diagnosed in earlier years counted here?

b.q: In Bendigo, a new treatment lets people with a long-term lung condition live many more years. The number of new cases each year stays the same. What happens to prevalence?
opts: It rises, because people stay in the count for longer
It stays the same, because new cases have not changed
It falls, because the treatment improves people's health
It falls, because prevalence counts only new cases
b.why: Prevalence counts all existing cases, so people who live longer with the condition stay in the count while new cases keep being added. Incidence stays the same, but prevalence rises. Better treatment does not remove people from the count unless they no longer have the condition.
b.clue: Think about how long each person stays in the count.

a.best: Incidence, because it counts only new cases in a year

b.best: It rises, because people stay in the count for longer
